text:
maria: seeing mass 502s from eu-west service-mesh starting ~09:10 UTC, correlated with cert fetch failures
devin: confirmed, mesh-proxy logs show KMS decrypt DENIED on tls key unwrap for svc-account 'svc-ingest-eu'
devin: snippet: `ERROR: kms:Decrypt failed: access denied (permission denied)`
alex: any recent RBAC/IAM changes?
maria: ops ticket shows a permissions rollback yesterday to tighten KMS key access for a group — might be related
jordan: adding logs from envoy side: `mTLS: tls_context/0 private_key unwrap error` then `downstream connection closed`
sre-bot: deploy-bot noticed a role binding change in eu-control-plane at 2026-03-18T22:45Z (PR #4521 merged) :warning:
maria: can someone check the KMS key policy and the k8s controller SA binding? quick hypothesis: controller lost decrypt on key used for node certs
devin: running quick IAM check now. if SA missing decrypt, that explains immediate failover across pods that try to rotate certs
kevin: pulling audit logs from KMS: `2026-03-18T22:46:01Z DecryptDenied principal=system:serviceaccount:ingress:mesh-controller reason=policy`
alex: that principal should be present in the key policy. looks like the recent RBAC tighten removed `mesh-controller` ASG binding from the project iam policy — not the key policy though. wonder if we have overlapping controls (project IAM + key policy) both gating decrypt
maria: securitybot, any alerts on missing audit fields? we've had issues where audit log entries lack the principal field due to export filtering
securitybot: noticed ~15% of KMS audit entries had truncated principal when exported to splunk between 22:40-22:55 UTC. raw stack logs retained full entries. export pipeline backpressure suspected
jordan: immediate mitigation options? fallback to regional backup key? or rebind the SA in key policy and roll certs slowly
devin: plan: 1) rebind SA -> key policy (fast, rollback-able) 2) restart mesh-controller pods to re-attempt unwrap 3) run smoke canary across a single AZ 4) monitor telemetry (error rate, p50 latency)
maria: do we have automation to rebind quickly? policy changes require infra-approver on call
kevin: I can push a temporary key-policy patch (manual) under my creds, will record request. doing it now. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
kevin: patched key policy to include serviceAccount:ingress/mesh-controller at 22:58Z
devin: restarting mesh-controller in eu-west canary pool now: `kubectl -n ingress rollout restart deploy/mesh-controller --context=eu-west`
sre-bot: rollout started, pod-ids: mesh-controller-5f7d and mesh-controller-5f8a
alex: after restart, envoy logs show successful unwrap and TLS context loaded for canary hosts. rolling to remaining nodes in AZ-1
maria: monitoring metrics: 502 rate dropped from 8% -> 0.6% in canary window, latency stable. good sign :thumbsup:
jordan: next: audit full cross-check for overlapping controls — key policy vs project IAM vs org restrictions. also need an incident ticket for vuln triage re: overly broad RBAC rollbacks causing availability impact
devin: documenting exact root cause: RBAC cleanup PR removed project-level IAM binding that transitively prevented key policy evaluation from granting decrypt? need to write concise causal chain for postmortem
kevin: posting minimal rollback playbook in infra runbook: steps to rebind SA, verify KMS decrypt, restart controller, validate handshake. will add commands:
kevin: ```
# verify KMS decrypt allowed for principal
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy KEY_NAME --location=global --format=json
# check audit log for principal deny
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="kms_key" AND protoPayload.methodName="Decrypt" AND severity="ERROR"' --limit 50
```
maria: checklist for postmortem: - timeline - PR that caused change + author - exact policy diff - impact metrics by region - remediation timeline - action owners
securitybot: recommending two action items: 1) add a CI gate that flags project IAM changes affecting KMS-scoped principals, 2) enrich export pipeline to avoid principal truncation during peak traffic
alex: +1 to CI gate. also add a live runbook link in key policies that lists emergency approvers and temporary patch pattern
jordan: question: do we rotate the affected keys as a precaution? might cause mass reconnects; prefer avoid if not compromised
maria: agree — no rotation unless we detect compromise. current evidence is policy-only. we'll avoid key rotation for now
devin: opening incident ticket INC-2026-033 with above plan, assigning owners: kevin (remediation), alex (postmortem write), jordan (runbook updates), maria (customer comms)
kevin: will follow up with RFC to change the RBAC cleanup process so it requires a cross-check against secrets/keys access maps
maria: thanks all. keep thread updates short — any regression ping here. closing canary window at 23:10 UTC if stable. :white_check_mark:
